Three criteria of SAM in children 6–59 months (any one)?
MUAC < 11.5 cm, weight-for-height < −3 SD, bilateral pitting oedema.
MUAC range of moderate acute malnutrition (MAM)?
Without oedema (marasmus) or with oedema (kwashiorkor); oedema + severe wasting is the most severe.
A child has a low weight-for-age but normal weight-for-height. Wasted?
No: underweight is not wasting; wasting = low weight-for-height.
A child has bilateral pitting oedema and a normal MUAC. Diagnosis?
SAM (oedematous malnutrition), whatever the weight or MUAC.
Dietary cause of SAM without oedema?
Deficiency of total energy (calories and protein): starvation.

Indications to admit a child with SAM?
Medical complication, failed appetite test, oedema +++, oedema with severe wasting, infant < 6 months not feeding well.
How is the appetite test done?
Child eats the RUTF test amount for his weight within 30 minutes = pass → OTP.
Treatment of hypoglycaemia in a conscious child with SAM?
50 ml of 10% glucose (or sugar water) orally or by NGT, then F-75.
Treatment of hypoglycaemia in an unconscious child with SAM?
10% glucose 5 ml/kg IV, then 50 ml by NGT.

Rehydration fluid in SAM without shock?
ReSoMal: 5 ml/kg every 30 min for 2 h, then 5–10 ml/kg/h for 4–10 h.
Na and K content of ReSoMal?
Na 45 and K 40 mmol/L (ORS: Na 75, K 20).

Treatment of severe anaemia (Hb < 4 g/dL) in SAM?

When is iron started in SAM?
In the rehabilitation phase (week 2), when the child gains weight.
When is high-dose vitamin A given in SAM, and the dose over 12 months?
